## D — Safe driving

Accuracy scope: every fact in Safe driving uses one physical page of the registered Kansas handbook, with original wording and one complete claim per block.
All quantities and exceptions are edition-bound. The cited handbook is the evidence; no recollection or competitor text supplies authority.
Source flags: City versus urban look-ahead distances, lane-change gaps, signal timing and horn-use scope conflict or lack distinctions. Hydroplaning thresholds are not safety guarantees. Some road-limit context spans pages. All disputed values remain explicit debt. [A56] [A57] [A58] [A59] [A60] [A61] [A62] [A63] [A64] [A65] [A66] [A67] [A68] [A69] [A70] [A71] [A72]
Refresh disposition: legal thresholds and administrative procedures require rechecking against an issuer source when a later edition replaces this snapshot.

corpus_stability.reason: The bound Kansas handbook has one February 2022 revision label; the selected source contains no evidence of multiple annual corpus rewrites. Later legal or administrative changes require issuer rechecking.

verification_debt.claim_text: Page 56 L27-29 gives city searching as two blocks/signals and urban searching as three blocks/signals without distinguishing city from urban. Neither number is taught as a universal urban rule; highway quarter-mile and 20-30-second visual-lead guidance are separately supported.

Page 60 L10-16 describes stable wet traction around 30 mph, rising on pooled water above 35 mph, total loss in heavy rain at 45-50 mph, and worn-tire loss at 25-30 mph. These are not established universal safe-speed or onset thresholds; retain all values for issuer clarification, with slowing on wet roads supported.
Page 60 L18-20 says same-direction vehicles at equal speeds with adequate spacing cannot hit one another. It omits changing conditions; do not teach this as a guarantee.

Page 58 L20-22 specifies a 4-5-second lane-change gap. Page 64 L29-35 and the page-72 answer key specify 4-6 seconds. Page 64 says moving into the middle enables both vehicles to adjust to three seconds, which is not guaranteed by a four-second gap. Preserve both ranges and the adjustment claim as unresolved; no unified numeric gap is invented.

The outside-town and otherwise-unposted normal-condition heading is on page 61 L39-45; page 62 L3-6 continues with 75 mph on separated multilane highways designated and posted by the Secretary, 65 mph State/Federal highways, and 55 mph county/township highways. Complete conditions span pages. Under the single-page fact contract these class defaults remain debt rather than unqualified legal rules.

Page 63 L37-42 says many states require 500 feet behind emergency equipment and gives minimum 12 seconds at 30 mph or six seconds at 60 mph. It does not establish a Kansas-specific 500-foot law; no such Kansas legal threshold is taught.

Page 68 L11-22 recommends light taps in ordinary conflict-warning situations and sharp blasts for danger, but L23-28 limits horn use to emergencies. The broad ordinary-use versus emergency-only distinction needs clarification; listed non-warning uses and danger warnings remain supported.

Page 69 L18-21 gives urban 100 feet or 3-5 seconds and above-40-mph 200 feet or 3-5 seconds; L39-41 gives at least 3-4 seconds. Do not substitute one precise universal signaling threshold or claim these are equivalent at every speed.

Page 57 L32-36 directs pulling into an intersection for a left turn without restating a signal or clear-path condition; page 47 L6-12 mentions green. The unconditional staging instruction is withheld; safe-gap and unobstructed-path requirements are supported.

Page 70 L25-26 says a license is needed for any vehicle on a public highway or parking facility, without the exemptions described earlier in the handbook. Do not use it as an exceptionless licensing rule.

The page-69 L22-28 A/B vehicle example refers to a previous-page illustration. Relative geometry and vehicle-specific interpretation are not established by the extracted text alone; the visual example remains debt.
